sections.title: Observed demand and A0 checks
text: Daily trips with SA-coded origin and A0 destination, one record per origin and date. Daily totals require all expected SA station counts.
Sum of counts to named station destinations, excluding A0. Missing or invalid records and duplicate keys are flagged.
The separately published rail_lrt_shah_alam count. Line attribution at interchanges follows the publisher's own methodology.

Bottom-up sum of the six distinct published Rapid Rail service series. The common history requires all components, with no implicit pre-service zeros. This is a service-count total. Journey-level transfer deduplication is unavailable.

Select a single destination A0 for each published origin and day when its unique present detail records cover its entire published destination roster and sum exactly to that subtotal. A0 origin records serve as a separate incoming check; neither type of aggregate is added to detail records.

sections.title: Model selection and rolling-origin evaluation
text: Model selection uses the arithmetic mean of horizon-specific WAPEs. Ties prefer the seasonal naive baseline.

Mature series use up to the most recent 730 days at each origin. Short series use available history since first positive observation. Sensitivity fits start August 15. Training-only gaps use prior same-weekday demand or the immediately prior value. Missing actuals are excluded from all metrics and zero actuals only from MAPE.
Last 28 calendar days weighted by each forecast window's weekday mix.
Original selections used 7-, 14- and 28-lead rolling scores. The active fixed-policy replay reports the already inspected terminal window separately. Overlapping origins can reuse observations.
Backtests use the selected published snapshot's historical observations. Point-in-time snapshots for each fold are unavailable.

sections.title: Cold-start, stability and feature experiments
text: Equal weights across five independently normalized donor profiles. The target's trailing 28 days set forecast level. Transfer weights are fixed in advance.
Full, trailing 56-day and August 15 boundary fits. The zero-drift reconstruction holds terminal level and weekly seasonal factors fixed.
All uses of the already inspected terminal holdout are retrospective.
C adds a scheduled holiday flag and a coverage indicator. Earlier years and tentative-only dates are unknown. Incremental scores cover the bundle.
Configurable planning thresholds. Demand change and uncertainty are separate. Forecast dates before or on the as-of date remain projections.
Lag and calendar predictors and observed demand patterns are non-causal. Fuel, labour and registration data were deferred from predictive modelling.
A single short terminal holdout and overlapping rolling residual dates cannot establish calibration. Leads 15–28 have no holdout points and no band extends past day 28.

sections.title: Holiday evidence and active forecasting policy
text: Observed holiday comparisons use dates verified in at least one extracted jurisdiction and controls with known non-holiday status. Tentative and uncovered dates are excluded from both samples.
Per-jurisdiction records and Sunday substitution provenance are retained. The archive cannot establish later gazettes or separate Putrajaya coverage.

Active Ridge forecasts and affected comparisons use the same verified-holiday indicator in fitting and prediction. Tentative and unknown statuses remain distinct in provenance. They receive no verified adjustment.

The release keeps the original model families, training policies and hyperparameters. Corrected metrics reuse the original dates and origins. The Step 2B ablation retains its separate holiday and coverage feature bundle.

The replay uses one archived calendar snapshot. Historical release and revision vintages are unavailable, and the terminal window had already been inspected. The replay does not establish fresh independent performance or 90-day accuracy.

sections.title: Scheduled reference and nominal supply
text: Count each journey's first-stop departure only. Exact schedules use a departure event. Frequency intervals contribute overlap seconds divided by headway seconds. Both directions add two terminal streams for the same route, without cross-route sums.

Future activity uses a fixed reference schedule. The archive contains no GTFS calendar_dates table. Dates flagged by the archived holiday calendar or without a covered holiday calendar have no paired dated supply.
Ratio of forecast published trips to reference two-direction departures on the same set of included days. Historical weekday-matched baseline uses the same denominator.
Terminal departures times editable nominal design places per three-car train. Estimates depend on train formation and reference service being delivered.

Saved Komuter hourly shares multiply daily OD scenarios. Network and Port Klang West, pooled and each observed year, are separate sensitivities. Each day retains all 24 bins. Peak windows sum the two matching hourly demand and supply values.
Station-origin demand has no directional or segment distribution. Supply remains separate from demand in the peak export. No occupancy or pressure ratio is calculated.

sections.title: District scope, mapping and thresholds
text: Eight whole administrative units used as a district proxy for districts referenced in the PLANMalaysia National Conurbation glossary. The planning extent encompasses parts of Selangor; whole districts enable consistent joins and denominators.
One unambiguous polygon interior contains the GTFS point; touching or overlapping matches are unresolved.
Shared trunk records and documented integrated interchange facilities are grouped. Separate structures connected by public walks retain separate station IDs.

Use the latest common survey year for all eight units and repeat for the newest locally available survey cohort. Linear unweighted district quantiles use inclusive comparisons. A priority requires low station density and the specified either/both household vulnerability condition. Observed LRT3 activity is contextual evidence only.
Observed counts describe trips published in this local tap-in/tap-out OD snapshot. Source-internal reconciliation is exact where reported and does not establish capture of every underlying journey.

Destination coverage is asymmetric. The published destination roster has substantially fewer Putrajaya Line codes than the origin roster. An absent OD pair is outside the observed roster, with no zero or trip estimate assigned.

Separate source origin codes at the same physical facility remain separate categories of published activity. The diagnostic checks for identical daily series. Transaction-level evidence would be needed to test partial overlap or transfer counting.
KTM, ERL, BRT and other modes are outside the Rapid Rail scope. Station-origin trips can include travellers from other districts, repeated trips by one person and transfers recorded by the source.

Per-resident figures scale origins by district population. Per-station figures are district averages over physical facilities. Neither metric measures congestion, walking access, resident modal share or unmet demand.

The historical Step 4 and 4B research used PLANMalaysia polygons. This publication independently assigns the GTFS points using the pinned OpenStreetMap polygons, then recomputes district activity, coverage and screening. Counts and classes agree with the archived results. Distance diagnostics are approximate and refer to the OpenStreetMap edges.

sections.title: SDG relevance
text: Demand and reference supply support discussion of reliable transport infrastructure under SDG 9. District access questions also relate to urban transport under SDG 11. The dashboard reports descriptive indicators for the available data.
